title: MATIZAR y ENFATIZAR
subtitle: Hedging and emphasis · suavizar y reforzar

map.center: Matizar (hedging) baja el volumen de una afirmación; enfatizar lo sube. Clave del inglés culto.

nodes.title: Énfasis gramatical
items: I did warn you! (¡Sí que te avisé!)

nodes.title: Consejo rápido
items: Un hedge por idea: no los acumules.

error.title: Error común
bad: It is supposed that prices will rise.
error.note: «Se supone que» → sujeto + is expected / supposed to

items.q: The data ___ to suggest a link.
a: appear
seem

items.q: I ___ lock the door, I promise!
items.a: did

items.a: far

items.q: There is no proof ___.
items.a: whatsoever

items.q: It's highly ___ to rain later.

explain.es: En el inglés culto, la fuerza de una afirmación se regula con precisión. Matizar (hedging) consiste en rebajar la rotundidad de lo que decimos —por prudencia científica, por cortesía o para protegernos de la crítica—: it would appear that…, arguably, to some extent. Enfatizar es lo contrario: reforzar una idea con recursos gramaticales y léxicos: I did warn you, by far, the very, whatsoever, utterly. Un hablante C2 maneja ambos como un control de volumen: ni todo es seguro ni todo es dudoso.
explain.en: Hedging <mark>tones down</mark> a claim (caution, politeness, academic precision); emphasis <mark>turns it up</mark>. A proficient writer controls both like a volume knob.

explain.title: Antes de empezar: el registro
explain.es: Académico y formal: it would appear, arguably, is thought to, highly, deeply, by far, whatsoever. Oral e informal: really, so, totally, kind of, sort of, I guess, loads better. No mezcles: The results are totally awesome no cabe en un ensayo. Para el énfasis por estructura (Never have I…, What matters is…) repasa C1-01 (inversión) y C1-02 (cleft sentences).
explain.en: Academic: it would appear, arguably, highly, by far. Informal: really, so, totally, kind of. Keep them apart.

explain.title: 1 · Verbos que matizan
explain.es: seem, appear y tend presentan la información como impresión o tendencia, no como un hecho probado. Con would la cautela aumenta: it would seem / it would appear that… es típico de artículos académicos e informes oficiales. Para referirnos al pasado usamos el infinitivo perfecto: appears to have + participio. También son verbos de cautela suggest, indicate y point to: los datos apuntan a, no demuestran.
explain.en: seem / appear / tend to present information as impression or tendency. Would adds extra caution. For the past: appear to have + past participle.
formula: It + *would seem / would appear* + that + oración

examples.en: The treatment appears to reduce symptoms in most patients.
examples.es: El tratamiento parece reducir los síntomas en la mayoría de los pacientes.

examples.en: It would seem that the original manuscript has been lost.
examples.es: Todo parece indicar que el manuscrito original se ha perdido.

examples.en: Investors tend to overreact to bad news.
examples.es: Los inversores tienden a reaccionar en exceso ante las malas noticias.

explain.title: 2 · Modales y probabilidad
explain.es: may, might y could rebajan la certeza; may well / could well equivalen a «es muy posible que». Para hablar de probabilidad con elegancia usamos be likely / unlikely to + infinitivo (¡nunca is probable to!) o there is a strong possibility that…. Should expresa lo que es razonable esperar: The results should be available by May.
explain.en: may / might / could lower certainty; may well = it is quite possible. Use be likely to, never be probable to. Should = what we reasonably expect.

examples.en: The strike may well spread to other sectors.
examples.es: Es muy posible que la huelga se extienda a otros sectores.

examples.en: Interest rates are unlikely to fall before the summer.
examples.es: Es poco probable que los tipos de interés bajen antes del verano.

examples.en: These findings could have important implications for policy.
examples.es: Estos hallazgos podrían tener implicaciones importantes para las políticas públicas.

explain.title: 3 · Distanciarse de la fuente
explain.es: Cuando no queremos responsabilizarnos de una afirmación, la atribuimos a otros con la pasiva impersonal (vista en B2), que aquí funciona como recurso de cautela: is thought / believed / said / reported / alleged to. Es la marca del periodismo prudente. Con adverbios: reportedly, allegedly, apparently, according to…. Allegedly (presuntamente) es imprescindible en noticias judiciales: informa sin acusar.
explain.en: Attribute a claim to others to keep your distance: is thought / said / reported / alleged to, reportedly, allegedly.
formula: Sujeto + *is thought / said / alleged* + to + infinitivo

examples.en: The fire is thought to have started in the kitchen.
examples.es: Se cree que el incendio empezó en la cocina.

examples.en: The senator allegedly accepted bribes from a construction firm.
examples.es: El senador presuntamente aceptó sobornos de una constructora.

examples.en: It is widely held that the reform came too late.
examples.es: Existe la opinión generalizada de que la reforma llegó demasiado tarde.

explain.title: La escala de certeza
head: Grado · Degree
Verbos y modales
Adverbios y adjetivos
Expresiones
Ejemplo · Example
rows: is likely to · there is a good chance
is unlikely to · it is doubtful whether
explain.note: Elige el grado que permiten tus datos. Pero no acumules hedges: It might possibly perhaps be the case… suena evasivo. Uno o dos por afirmación es suficiente.
explain.note_en: Choose the degree your evidence allows, but don't stack hedges: one or two per claim is enough.

explain.title: 4 · Adverbios y aproximadores
explain.es: arguably = «podría decirse que» (defendible, pero no indiscutible); presumably = «es de suponer que» (deducción lógica); apparently / seemingly = «al parecer, aparentemente»; conceivably = «cabe la posibilidad». Para limitar el alcance: to some / a certain extent, in part, on the whole, broadly speaking, in most cases. Con cifras, los aproximadores: approximately, roughly, some + número, in the region of, upwards of.
explain.en: arguably, presumably, apparently soften claims; to some extent, on the whole limit their scope; approximately, roughly, some soften figures.

examples.en: This is arguably the finest film of the decade.
examples.es: Podría decirse que es la mejor película de la década.

examples.en: To some extent, the crisis was self-inflicted.
examples.es: Hasta cierto punto, la crisis fue autoinfligida.

examples.en: The project will cost in the region of £40 million.
examples.es: El proyecto costará alrededor de 40 millones de libras.

explain.title: 5 · DO / DID enfático
explain.es: En una oración afirmativa, añadir do / does / did (acentuado al hablar) delante del infinitivo refuerza la verdad de lo dicho. Sirve para contradecir (I did lock the door!), insistir o conceder (He does have a point.) y, en imperativos, para una invitación cálida y algo formal (Do sit down.). Equivale a «sí que…», «de verdad», «claro que». El verbo va siempre en infinitivo sin to: I did told you.
explain.en: do / does / did + bare infinitive (stressed) adds emphasis: contradicting, insisting, conceding, or warm imperatives (Do come in).
formula: Sujeto + *do / does / did* + infinitivo sin to

examples.en: I did send the report — check your spam folder.
examples.es: Sí que mandé el informe: mira en la carpeta de spam.

examples.en: The theory does have its limitations, admittedly.
examples.es: Hay que reconocer que la teoría sí tiene sus limitaciones.
Sírvase café, por favor, con toda confianza.

explain.title: 6 · The very, -self, whatsoever, -ever
explain.es: the very + sustantivo = «justo, mismísimo, mero»: the very thought (la mera idea), at that very moment (en ese preciso instante). El reflexivo enfático subraya la identidad: the CEO herself = la propia directora. En negativas, «en absoluto»: no + sustantivo + whatsoever (siempre detrás), not… at all, not in the least. En preguntas de sorpresa: Whatever / However…?, Why ever…? = «¿pero qué / cómo…?».
explain.en: the very + noun = exact / mere; emphatic -self; no … whatsoever, not … at all; surprise: Whatever…? Why ever…?

examples.en: The very idea of moving abroad terrified her.
examples.es: La mera idea de mudarse al extranjero la aterraba.

examples.en: The company has shown no interest whatsoever in our proposal.
examples.es: La empresa no ha mostrado interés alguno por nuestra propuesta.

examples.en: The Prime Minister herself opened the debate.
examples.es: La propia primera ministra abrió el debate.
¿Pero qué te llevó a decir eso?

explain.title: VERY o ABSOLUTELY
explain.es: Los adjetivos graduables (good, cold, tired) admiten very / extremely / incredibly. Los extremos o absolutos (perfect, freezing, unique, exhausted) ya expresan el máximo: solo admiten absolutely / utterly / totally / completely. Really vale para ambos. Quite cambia de significado: quite good = bastante bueno; quite extraordinary = absolutamente extraordinario.
explain.en: Gradable adjectives take very / extremely; extreme or absolute ones take absolutely / utterly / totally. Quite = fairly (gradable) or completely (absolute).

explain.title: Intensificadores y sus collocations
head: Intensificador
Se combina con
Ejemplo · Example
Español
rows: I am fully aware of the risks.
It is vitally important to act now.
explain.note: Son collocations fijas: highly moved, deeply recommended o bitterly aware suenan extraños a un nativo. By far va delante del superlativo; delante de un comparativo, far / much: by far better → far better.
explain.note_en: These are fixed collocations. By far + superlative; far / much + comparative.

explain.title: Rotundo o académico
explain.es: El inglés académico y el periodismo de calidad prefieren afirmaciones calibradas: no dicen menos, dicen exactamente lo que los datos permiten. Compara cada afirmación rotunda con su versión matizada.
explain.en: Academic and quality journalistic English calibrate every claim to the evidence.

cols.head: 🎓 Matizado · hedged
items: Heavy social media use may contribute to depression among teenagers.
It would appear that the policy has not achieved its aims.
There is growing evidence that most diets tend to fail in the long term.
The author's argument is, arguably, flawed in several respects.

explain.title: Texto modelo: un abstract
explain.es: Fíjate en cómo este resumen de un artículo científico combina cautela (en azul) con énfasis (en rojo) allí donde la evidencia es sólida. «Este estudio examina… Los resultados parecen indicar que hablar dos idiomas desde la infancia puede, hasta cierto punto, retrasar el deterioro cognitivo. El efecto fue, con diferencia, más acusado entre… Aunque la muestra es relativamente pequeña, los datos sí respaldan…»
explain.en: This study examines the relationship between early bilingualism and cognitive ageing. The results would appear to suggest that speaking two languages from childhood may, to some extent, delay the onset of age-related decline. The effect was by far the most pronounced among participants who used both languages daily. Although the sample is relatively small and the findings should be interpreted with caution, the data do support the view that bilingualism is highly unlikely to be cognitively neutral.

explain.title: ¿Cómo calibro una afirmación?
explain.title_en: How do I calibrate a claim?

items.en: Pick one device of the right degree.

items.es: ¿No es tu afirmación? Distánciate: is thought to, reportedly.
items.en: Not your claim? Keep your distance.

items.es: Limita el alcance: to some extent, in most cases.
Si la evidencia es sólida, enfatiza: by far, the data do show.
Relee: ¿más de dos hedges por frase? Elimina los sobrantes.

items.en: Some readers may find the ending somewhat abrupt.

items.en: The figures are, broadly speaking, in line with expectations.

items.en: It was by far the most difficult decision of my career.

items.en: The new engine is far more efficient than its predecessor.

items.en: I do wish you had told me earlier.

items.en: She was utterly devastated by the news.

items.en: However did you manage to get tickets?

I am totally agree with you.

items.why: Calco y exceso de hedges: suena evasivo.

items.q: Very unique is acceptable in formal writing.

items.q: Emphatic do / does / did is followed by the bare infinitive.
By far is typically placed before a superlative: by far the best.
Whatsoever is normally used in affirmative sentences.
items.why: It follows no / any / nothing in negative contexts.

items.q: Presumably expresses absolute certainty.
items.why: It expresses a logical assumption: «es de suponer».

items.q: Arguably means that a claim is probably false.
items.why: It means the claim can reasonably be defended.

items.q: Stacking several hedges in one sentence can make a writer sound evasive.
Highly collocates naturally with likely, recommended and qualified.
Quite impossible means «bastante imposible».
items.why: With absolute adjectives, quite = completely: «del todo imposible».

items.q: The very + noun means «muy» + noun.
items.why: It means «justo, mismísimo, mero»: the very moment.

items.q: Is probable to + infinitive is incorrect.
items.why: Use is likely to or it is probable that.

exercises.text_title: Does remote work really make us more productive?
text: Few workplace changes have been as rapid, or as hotly debated, as the shift to remote working. Early studies appeared to show that employees working from home were, on the whole, more productive than their office-based colleagues. More recent research, however, would seem to paint a rather more complicated picture.

According to a large survey published last year, productivity tends to rise for routine, individual tasks but may well fall when work depends on close collaboration. Managers, for their part, are thought to underestimate the output of staff they cannot see. The survey is by far the most comprehensive to date, yet its authors themselves concede that their conclusions are, to some extent, provisional.

What the data do show, quite unambiguously, is that employees value flexibility above almost everything else. Arguably, the very notion of a fixed nine-to-five day has been called into question. Whether companies will embrace this is, presumably, a matter of trust rather than technology. There is no evidence whatsoever that forcing staff back to the office five days a week improves results — although, as one economist drily put it, ‘absence of evidence is not evidence of absence’.

items.q: Early studies suggested that home workers were generally more productive.
The survey found that productivity rises for highly collaborative work.
items.why: It tends to rise for routine, individual tasks and may well fall for collaborative work.

items.q: The authors present their conclusions as final.
items.why: They concede their conclusions are, to some extent, provisional.

items.q: There is clear evidence that full-time office attendance improves results.
items.why: There is no evidence whatsoever that it does.

items.q: Find three hedging expressions in paragraph 1.
items.a: appeared to show · on the whole · would seem to · rather

items.q: Which phrase in paragraph 2 reports a belief without the writer endorsing it?
items.a: are thought to (underestimate)

items.q: Find four devices of emphasis in the text.
items.a: by far · themselves · do show · quite unambiguously · the very notion · whatsoever

items.q: Why does the writer use presumably in paragraph 3?
items.a: To present a logical inference, not a proven fact.

items.q: What does the economist's remark add to the final claim?
items.a: A further hedge: the lack of evidence does not prove that office attendance never improves results.

items.q: Es muy posible que la reunión se aplace.
a: The meeting may well be postponed.
The meeting could well be postponed.

items.q: Se cree que el cuadro fue pintado en Sevilla.
a: The painting is believed to have been painted in Seville.
The picture is thought to have been painted in Seville.

items.q: Es, con diferencia, el mejor restaurante de la ciudad.
a: It is by far the best restaurant in the city.
It is by far the best restaurant in town.

items.q: ¡Sí que te avisé!
items.a: I did warn you!

items.q: No tengo intención alguna de dimitir.
a: I have no intention whatsoever of resigning.
I have no intention of resigning at all.

items.q: Eres justo la persona que estaba buscando.
items.a: You are the very person I was looking for.

items.q: La propia ministra reconoció el error.
a: The minister herself acknowledged the mistake.
The minister herself admitted the mistake.

items.q: Hasta cierto punto, la crisis era previsible.
a: To some extent, the crisis was foreseeable.
To a certain extent, the crisis was predictable.

items.q: Estaba profundamente preocupada por las consecuencias.
items.a: She was deeply concerned about the consequences.

exercises.title: Ahora escribe tú
exercises.es: Escribe frases propias. Cuida el registro: académico, periodístico o formal.
exercises.en: Write your own sentences. Mind the register.

items.q: Matiza esta afirmación con al menos dos hedges: Video games cause violence.
items.a: Ej.: There would appear to be some evidence that violent video games may, in certain cases, contribute to aggressive behaviour.

items.q: Contradice con do / did enfático: You never listen to me.
items.a: Ej.: I do listen to you — I just don't always agree with you.

items.q: Escribe sobre tu ciudad con by far + superlativo y un adjetivo extremo con absolutely.
items.a: Ej.: Granada is by far the most beautiful city I know; the Alhambra at sunset is absolutely breathtaking.

items.q: Escribe la primera frase de un informe con It would appear that y to some extent.
items.a: Ej.: It would appear that, to some extent, the new timetable has improved punctuality.

items.q: Escribe una frase de queja formal con deeply y whatsoever.
items.a: Ej.: I am deeply disappointed that I have received no explanation whatsoever for the delay.

items.q: Redacta una noticia breve (2 frases) con allegedly y is thought to.
items.a: Ej.: The businessman allegedly transferred €2 million to an offshore account. He is thought to have left the country last week.

exercises.title: Transformaciones (Cambridge C2)
exercises.es: Completa la segunda frase para que signifique lo mismo que la primera. Usa la palabra clave (entre paréntesis) sin cambiarla y entre 3 y 8 palabras.
exercises.en: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the key word unchanged and 3–8 words.

items.q:
People believe that the painting was stolen in 1911.
→ The painting ________ in 1911.
items.a: The painting is believed to have been stolen in 1911.

items.q:
It seems that the company has underestimated the risks.
→ The company ________ the risks.
items.a: The company appears to have underestimated the risks.

items.q:
No other restaurant in town is anywhere near as good as this one.
→ This is ________ restaurant in town.
items.a: This is by far the best restaurant in town. / This is far and away the best restaurant in town.

items.q:
He showed absolutely no remorse.
→ He showed ________.
items.a: He showed no remorse whatsoever.

items.q:
You're right that I promised to call you, but I forgot.
→ I ________ you, but I forgot.
items.a: I did promise to call you, but I forgot.

items.q:
It is highly probable that the talks will collapse within days.
→ The talks ________ within days.
items.a: The talks are highly likely to collapse within days. / The talks are very likely to collapse within days.

items.q:
Just thinking about the exam made me nervous.
→ The ________ the exam made me nervous.
items.a: The very thought of the exam made me nervous.

items.q:
Apparently, the minister knew nothing about the deal.
→ The minister ________ nothing about the deal.
items.a: The minister seems to have known nothing about the deal.

checklist.es: Sé matizar con seem, appear, tend to y it would appear that.
checklist.en: I can hedge with seem, appear, tend to and it would appear that.

checklist.es: Gradúo la certeza con may well, is likely to, presumably, arguably.
checklist.en: I can grade certainty with may well, is likely to, presumably, arguably.

checklist.es: Me distancio de una fuente con is thought to, allegedly, reportedly.
checklist.en: I can distance myself from a source.

checklist.es: Uso el do / did enfático, the very, el -self enfático y whatsoever.
checklist.en: I use emphatic do, the very, emphatic -self and whatsoever.

checklist.es: Combino intensificadores con naturalidad: highly likely, deeply moved, by far the best.
Nunca escribo <s>very unique</s>, <s>is probable to</s> ni <s>It is supposed that</s>.
checklist.en: I never write very unique, is probable to or It is supposed that.

checklist.es: Ajusto el registro: no sobre-matizo ni uso so / really / totally en textos académicos.
checklist.en: I adjust the register: no over-hedging, no informal intensifiers in academic texts.
